Convert desalination electricity inputs

Skill: genesis-convert-energy-units

Reverse osmosis electricity inputs: 1971: 12 kWh/m³; 2015: 2.75 kWh/m³; 2017: 2.75 kWh/m³; 2100: 1.75 kWh/m³.

Read 1 of 1 match. A recorded replay at registry revision 2026-11-21, not current data.

Limits of this example
  • These are global model coefficients, not measurements at a desalination plant. The seawater input is a separate row and is not converted.

Run this example locally

After installing DOE-MCP, replay without a key, model or network request:

doe-mcp demo world-desalination-electricity --output ./demo-output

Add --live to query publishers. No model is called. Live results and availability can differ.

Inspect blanks in emissions coefficients

Skill: genesis-audit-coefficient-gaps

Among 39 technology rows, 18 CO coefficients are blank, 0 are explicitly zero, and 21 are nonzero.

Read 39 of 39 matches. A recorded replay at registry revision 2026-11-21, not current data.

Limits of this example
  • A blank is not zero. Exception fields are retained but not resolved; this file gives no physical unit for the coefficients.

Read 35 of 35 matches. A recorded replay at registry revision 2026-11-21, not current data.

Limits of this example
  • Lifetime is the cohort maximum; half-life belongs to a particular retirement function. A blank half-life gives no retirement date or proof that the function runs.

Publisher table notes and units
  • File: A23.globaltech_retirement.csv
  • Title: Electricity technology retirement parameters
  • Units: Years for lifetime and half.life; Unitless for shutdown.rate; steepness; median.shutdown.point; profit.shutdown.steepness
  • Source: GCAM assumptions; generally consistent with other models
  • Comments: lifetime: maximum lifetime of cohort. If no retirement function is used; the entire cohort is retired in this number of years.
  • shutdown.rate: portion of cohort retired each year; used by the phased-shutdown-decider retirement function.
  • half.life: number of years at which 50% of the cohort is retired; using the s-curve-shutdown-decider retirement function.
  • steepness: shape parameter used by the s-curve-shutdown-decider retirement function.
  • median.shutdown.point: Profit-ratio ((revenue - costs) / costs) at which 50% of cohort is shut down by profit shutdown decider. Only variable costs.
  • profit.shutdown.steepness: shape parameter of profit-shutdown-decider function.
  • Column types: ccccicnnni

    "source_notes": [
      "File: A23.globaltech_retirement.csv",
      "Title: Electricity technology retirement parameters",
      "Units: Years for lifetime and half.life; Unitless for shutdown.rate; steepness; median.shutdown.point; profit.shutdown.steepness",
      "Source: GCAM assumptions; generally consistent with other models",
      "Comments: lifetime: maximum lifetime of cohort. If no retirement function is used; the entire cohort is retired in this number of years.",
      "shutdown.rate: portion of cohort retired each year; used by the phased-shutdown-decider retirement function.",
      "half.life: number of years at which 50% of the cohort is retired; using the s-curve-shutdown-decider retirement function.",
      "steepness: shape parameter used by the s-curve-shutdown-decider retirement function.",
      "median.shutdown.point: Profit-ratio ((revenue - costs) / costs) at which 50% of cohort is shut down by profit shutdown decider. Only variable costs.",
      "profit.shutdown.steepness: shape parameter of profit-shutdown-decider function.",
      "Column types: ccccicnnni",
      "----------"
    ],

Compare crop yield assumptions

Skill: genesis-compare-fallback-rates

The fallback rate changes for 11 of 18 commodities between 2050 and 2095.

Read 18 of 18 matches. A recorded replay at registry revision 2026-11-21, not current data.

Limits of this example
  • GCAM uses fallback rates where regional crop estimates are unavailable and beyond 2050. These rates are not harvested yields.

Account for uncaptured carbon

Skill: genesis-compute-residual-shares

The uncaptured share is lower in 2100 than in the initial future year for 6 of 6 technology rows.

Read 6 of 6 matches. A recorded replay at registry revision 2026-11-21, not current data.

Limits of this example
  • A fraction of a technology’s CO₂ stream gives neither tonnes emitted nor a lifecycle emissions estimate.

Compare geothermal heat across regions

Skill: genesis-compare-resource-grades

Across 14 legacy regions, grade 2 heat inputs range from 0.001 to 10.23454 thermal EJ per year.

Read 14 of 14 matches. A recorded replay at registry revision 2026-11-21, not current data.

Limits of this example
  • These inputs are heat available to power plants, in thermal EJ per year. They do not measure generated electricity.

Download JSON evidenceDownload CSV evidence indexDownload worksheet CSV

Run this example locally

After installing DOE-MCP, replay without a key, model or network request:

doe-mcp demo world-geothermal-grades --output ./demo-output

Add --live to query publishers. No model is called. Live results and availability can differ.

Soil carbon recovery in Kenya

Skill: trace-soil-carbon

GCAM assigns a soil carbon recovery time of 25 years to the region containing Kenya.

Read 1 of 1 match. A recorded replay at registry revision 2026-11-21, not current data.

Limits of this example
  • The regional parameter describes recovery after land-use change. It is not a measurement from a Kenyan field.

Download JSON evidenceDownload CSV evidence index

Run this example locally

After installing DOE-MCP, replay without a key, model or network request:

doe-mcp demo kenya-soil --output ./demo-output

Add --live to query publishers. No model is called. Live results and availability can differ.

      "description": "This Final Technical Report summarizes work completed under Award Number DEEE0009833, titled \"Low-cost, Highly Efficient and Fast Thermally Pressed Scalable Carbon-based Planar Perovskite Solar Cells.\" The project addressed the central technical problem that carbon-electrode perovskite solar cells (C-PSCs) can reduce electrode costs and improve environmental durability, but they have historically lagged noble-metalcontact devices due to poor carbon/perovskite contact, high carbon-electrode resistance, imperfect hole extraction, and insufficient operational stability. The Statement of Project Objectives (SOPO), therefore, required systematic engineering of thermally pressed carbon-based planar perovskite solar cells by improving the carbon/perovskite interface quality, improving carbon-electrode conductivity, and further increasing device stability. The work advanced understanding of carbon-based perovskite photovoltaics by connecting device performance to three coupled mechanisms: interfacial recombination at the perovskite/hole-transport-layer/carbon stack; lateral and vertical transport losses in carbon contacts; and instability driven by moisture, heat, illumination, ion migration, and slow/variable manufacturing steps.",

3 DOE PAGES records for a bibliography. The worksheet marks how many authors each catalog summary omitted.

Limits of this example
  • Only the first DOE PAGES results page was read. No full text or citation counts were retrieved.
  • Author strings come from the catalog. Check omitted authors against the publisher before citing.

After installing DOE-MCP, replay without a key, model or network request:

doe-mcp demo bibliography --output ./demo-output

Add --live to query publishers. No model is called. Live results and availability can differ.

The missing Daymet date

Skill: genesis-package-weather-data

Requested 2024-12-26 through 2024-12-31. Daymet returned 5 daily maxima, ending 2024-12-30. Its leap-year calendar ends on December 30.

A recorded replay at registry revision 2026-11-21, not current data.

Limits of this example
  • Daymet models the 1 km grid cell around the requested point. These are not station readings.
  • The CSV contains only the returned dates. A missing date has no temperature value.

Download JSON evidenceDownload CSV evidence indexDownload temperatures CSVDownload Croissant metadata

The Genesis Croissant skill describes how to document a CSV. Download both files into one directory. The Croissant file names each column and gives the SHA-256 checksum of the temperature CSV.

Run this example locally

After installing DOE-MCP, replay without a key, model or network request:

doe-mcp demo daymet-calendar --output ./demo-output

Check a load prediction band

Skill: genesis-check-prediction-bands

The 90th percentile of the first 15 absolute errors was 62 MW. A band that far either side of the prior reading covered 7 of the next 8 readings.

A recorded replay at registry revision 2026-11-21, not current data.

Limits of this example
  • The band uses the nearest-rank percentile of earlier errors. Later readings do not set its width.
  • Coverage describes this short window. Serially related readings do not establish a future coverage guarantee.

Five-minute BPA load prediction

Skill: genesis-score-load-errors

Each prediction uses the preceding load reading. Across 11 five-minute comparisons, the mean absolute error was 28.91 MW and the root mean squared error was 36.98 MW.

A recorded replay at registry revision 2026-11-21, not current data.

Limits of this example
  • The prediction repeats the prior reading. BPA supplied the load measurements, not these predictions.
  • The scores describe this window alone. No model was trained and no prediction interval was estimated.
  • Pairs must be five minutes apart on the publisher’s Pacific clock. Blank load values do not count as zero.

Microbiome study and sample finder

Skill: microbiome-data-finder

Followed one returned study. Showing 5 biosamples out of 23 matches.

Read 1 of 1 match. A recorded replay at registry revision 2026-11-21, not current data.

Limits of this example
  • Study and sample metadata only; no sequences, assemblies or annotations were downloaded.
  • At most five samples are shown; they do not establish study completeness or biological function.
  • The publisher's access recipes distinguish dataset DOIs from award DOIs; a DOI alone does not establish free access.

Download JSON evidenceDownload CSV evidence index

Run this example locally

After installing DOE-MCP, replay without a key, model or network request:

doe-mcp demo microbiome --output ./demo-output

Add --live to query publishers. No model is called. Live results and availability can differ.

  • No published rate limit, same as the rest of the OSTI family.

Releases covering the requested year

  • EAGLE-I Power Outage Data 2014 - 2022
    Published: 2023-05-25

How to interpret the data

  • EAGLE-I Power Outage Data Information
    Published: 2023-05-25

Customer denominator — check its vintage

  • EAGLE-I County Customer Dataset Fall 2025
    Published: 2026-05-05

Catalog records for EAGLE-I's annual releases, not outage numbers. Each release is a set of county-level files of customers without power at 15-minute intervals behind its DOI. Customers out is not people out, coverage is roughly 92% of US customers with small utilities and cooperatives missing, and the county customer-count dataset is the denominator for a share-of-customers figure. That dataset is a snapshot dated in its own title, so a share for a different year mixes vintages.

Publisher access recipes

  • EAGLE-I Power Outage Data 2014 - 2022 — The files are held at ORNL's repository behind this DOI; returned as data and never fetched here.
  • EAGLE-I County Customer Dataset Fall 2025 — The files are held at ORNL's repository behind this DOI; returned as data and never fetched here.
  • EAGLE-I Power Outage Data Information — The files are held at ORNL's repository behind this DOI; returned as data and never fetched here.

Does DOE publish this?

Skill: find-doe-data

NREL resolves to National Laboratory of the Rockies, renamed 2025-12-01. 2 of 4 DOE catalogs returned geothermal records; the empty ones are older harvests.

Read 2 of 1,062 from DOE Data Explorer; 2 of 17 from Open Energy Data Hub (ORNL); 0 of 0 from DOE Open Data Catalog (data.json); 0 of 0 from DOE Software Inventory (code.json). A recorded replay at registry revision 2026-11-21, not current data.

Limits of this example
  • NREL is now the National Laboratory of the Rockies; nrel.gov has no DNS, so an old link or acronym can return nothing without an error.
  • Two of the four catalogs are harvested files with an old newest entry; zero matches there is not evidence that DOE holds nothing.
  • Registry sources marked proposed were named, not queried.

Download JSON evidenceDownload CSV evidence index

Run this example locally

After installing DOE-MCP, replay without a key, model or network request:

doe-mcp demo find-data --output ./demo-output

Add --live to query publishers. No model is called. Live results and availability can differ.

A recorded replay at registry revision 2026-11-21, not current data.

Limits of this example
  • One facility. ALCF and OLCF are registered and not read here; their absence says nothing about whether they are up.
  • Status is not queue position, allocation or permission to run a job.
  • The board's timestamps carry no time zone, and updated_at is the last change, not the last check. This is a recorded board, not current status.

Download JSON evidenceDownload CSV evidence index

Run this example locally

After installing DOE-MCP, replay without a key, model or network request:

doe-mcp demo facility-status --output ./demo-output

Add --live to query publishers. No model is called. Live results and availability can differ.

        "source_id": "alcf-status",
        "name": "ALCF computing status",
        "why_not_read": "Blocked probe. The status page is an Angular application and its data paths return HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare challenge to a scripted client, which under decision 0007 is blocked_probe and NOT gated: a WAF refusing this client shape says nothing about whether the data is public. One real-browser check, watching the application's own network calls, would settle both the endpoint and the posture. Joins the blocked-probe backlog. Note, 2026-10-20. One plain GET of the status page answered 200 with the application shell, so the 403 did not recur; one probe from one machine is not evidence that the posture changed. The page's own data path was found and is not a candidate: it is undocumented and carries queued and running job records, which this project does not read for any facility. ALCF documents a separate machine route, its implementation of the IRI Facility API at api.alcf.anl.gov, whose status reads answered a plain GET with JSON. Under decision 0025 that is a different source with its own terms, and it waits on a terms review before it is registered; this manifest stays proposed until then."
      },
      {
        "source_id": "olcf-status",
        "name": "OLCF center status",
        "why_not_read": "No machine interface found. status.olcf.ornl.gov does not resolve in DNS; the center-status page is a 1.5 KB stub; and the lab site's WordPress API exposes only WordPress's own routes, where /wp/v2/statuses is post statuses rather than system status. The next step is asking OLCF whether one exists rather than guessing at more paths."
      }

      "description": "This Final Technical Report summarizes work completed under Award Number DEEE0009833, titled \"Low-cost, Highly Efficient and Fast Thermally Pressed Scalable Carbon-based Planar Perovskite Solar Cells.\" The project addressed the central technical problem that carbon-electrode perovskite solar cells (C-PSCs) can reduce electrode costs and improve environmental durability, but they have historically lagged noble-metalcontact devices due to poor carbon/perovskite contact, high carbon-electrode resistance, imperfect hole extraction, and insufficient operational stability. The Statement of Project Objectives (SOPO), therefore, required systematic engineering of thermally pressed carbon-based planar perovskite solar cells by improving the carbon/perovskite interface quality, improving carbon-electrode conductivity, and further increasing device stability. The work advanced understanding of carbon-based perovskite photovoltaics by connecting device performance to three coupled mechanisms: interfacial recombination at the perovskite/hole-transport-layer/carbon stack; lateral and vertical transport losses in carbon contacts; and instability driven by moisture, heat, illumination, ion migration, and slow/variable manufacturing steps.",

Environmental study brief

Skill: environmental-study-brief

Permafrost dataset results and five days of modelled Oak Ridge weather are shown separately. No study-site match is established.

Read 5 of 329 matches. A recorded replay at registry revision 2026-11-21, not current data.

Limits of this example
  • The dataset search and Oak Ridge weather example are independent; no geographic or temporal relationship is asserted.
  • Daymet values are modelled grid-cell estimates, not station observations.

doe-mcp demo earth --output ./demo-output

Add --live to query publishers. No model is called. Live results and availability can differ.

Species not fully identified in all cases, but include samples from the genera: Alnus, Arctagrostis, Arctophila, Arctostaphylos, Betula, Carex, Eriophorum, Petasites, Picea, Populus, Rubus, Salix, Saxifraga and Vaccinium. Locations along the Council, Kougarok and Teller roads, Seward Peninsula, Alaska. Samples were collected from various locations as part of reconnaissance field work prior to establishment of formal NGEE Arctic study sites between August 22, 2014 and August 24, 2014. There is a single datafile in .csv format. The Next-Generation Ecosystem Experiments: Arctic (NGEE Arctic), was a research effort to reduce uncertainty in Earth System Models by developing a predictive understanding of carbon-rich Arctic ecosystems and feedbacks to climate. NGEE Arctic was supported by the Department of Energy's Office of Biological and Environmental Research. The NGEE Arctic project had two field research sites: 1) located within the Arctic polygonal tundra coastal region on the Barrow Environmental Observatory (BEO) and the North Slope near Utqiagvik (Barrow), Alaska and 2) multiple areas on the discontinuous permafrost region of the Seward Peninsula north of Nome, Alaska. Through observations, experiments, and synthesis with existing datasets, NGEE Arctic provided an enhanced knowledge base for multi-scale modeling and contributed to improved process representation at global pan-Arctic scales within the Department of Energy's Earth system Model (the Energy Exascale Earth System Model, or E3SM), and specifically within the E3SM Land Model component (ELM).",

During incubations, CO2 and CH4 concentrations and stable isotopes were determined by isotope ratio mass spectrometry. Porewater samples were collected from the S1 Bog (April 2015), a Sphagnum-dominated site at northern Minnesota peatland in the Marcell Experimental Forest, using permanently-installed piezometers, which provided profiles from the watertable surface to 200 cm depth. This is the site of the SPRUCE experiment. Porewater and peat samples were collected in July 2015 from an additional Sphagnum-dominated site within Stordalen Mire, Sweden, a palsa mire underlain by thawing permafrost, using perforated stainless steel tubes that were inserted into the peat to the desired depths (13 cm and 32 cm). Porewater samples were analyzed by Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FTICRMS) followed by Kendrick mass transform analysis. The Kendrick mass (i.e., Kendrick 1963) transform analysis identifies the gain or loss of specific chemical moieties (e.g. CH2, H2, CH2O, etc.) via mass differences, and was used to infer potential microbial degradation pathways by which compounds were consumed in these samples. Increasing depth would suggest more degradation of DOM with the greater length of time for peat accumulation and similarly, with increasing length of peat incubation.         "description": "This dataset is a model archive of the paper Permafrost Thaw, Uneven Subsidence and Projected Drying of Ice-wedge Polygon Tundra (in prep) to support a modeling study investigating how projected increases in Arctic temperature and precipitation will jointly influence hydrologic conditions in ice-rich tundra landscapes. With this dataset, this study is to address the research question: Will Arctic tundra landscapes become wetter or drier with increasing precipitation and temperature in the future when thaw-induced ground subsidence and associated microtopographic evolution are represented? The simulations focus on ice-wedge polygon tundra, a widespread form of ice-rich permafrost terrain that is highly sensitive to thaw-driven landscape change. This dataset contains model input and output data for four study watersheds in Alaska: Anaktuvuk, Utqiagvik (formerly Barrow), Brooks Foothills, and Prudhoe Bay. Simulations were performed using the Advanced Terrestrial Simulator (ATS, v1.5), a physics-rich integrated surface\u2013subsurface hydrologic model. For each watershed, ten modeling cases were performed representing two landscape evolution conditions (with subsidence and without subsidence) combined with five climate forcing scenarios derived from Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP5, SSP5 with precipitation trend, SSP2, SSP2 with precipitation trend, and SSP2 with double precipitation trend). Particularly, for each watershed under the forcing SSP2 with precipitation trend, there are two additional simulations considering spatially heterogeneous subsidence distributions: one assumes randomly distributed scaling and the other includes elevation dependent distribution scaling. These simulations span 1980\u20132099 and include spin-up runs (1980\u20132009) followed by transient projections (2010\u20132099). To facilitate reproducibility of simulations, all datasets are organized by watershed. For each study watershed, the dataset contains: (1) Pre-partitioned mesh files for 32-core modeling (.par.32.XX), located in EACH_WATERSHED/mesh/basin; and also a non-partitioned mesh file (.exo) located in EACH_WATERSHED/mesh; (2) Climate forcings corresponding to the five SSP scenarios (.h5), located in EACH_WATERSHED/data; (3) Final states (.h5) from column spin-up modeling used to initialize historical watershed-scale spin-up runs from 1980 to 2009, located in EACH_WATERSHED/PreSpinupHistorical; (4) Final states (.h5) of historical watershed-scale spin-up runs from 1980 to 2009 used to initialize projection runs, located in EACH_WATERSHED/Spinup_daymetERA5; (5) ATS modeling input files (.xml), located in EACH_WATERSHED/EACH_SIMULATION_SCENARIO/inputfiles; (6) ATS modeling output files (.dat), located in in EACH_WATERSHED/EACH_SIMULATION_SCENARIO/combined_obs; (7) For the Brooks Foothills watershed, additional spatial model outputs are provided (.h5) for selected years (2033 and 2093) used to generate spatial figures in this study, located in Brooksfoothills/EACH_SIMULATION_SCENARIO/results-WITH/WITHOUT_SUBSIDENCE-year2033/2093. All data files with suffix .h5 can be accessible through Python h5py, and all data files with suffix of .dat can be imported by Python pandas. Mesh file with .exo can be visualized through Paraview or read by Python netCDF. The Next-Generation Ecosystem Experiments in the Arctic (NGEE Arctic) project is a research effort to reduce uncertainty in the Department of Energy\u2019s Energy Exascale Earth System Model (E3SM) by developing a predictive understanding of Arctic tundra ecosystems underlain by permafrost and to quantify feedbacks from the Arctic tundra to the Earth system. NGEE Arctic is supported by the Department of Energy's Office of Biological and Environmental Research. Over Phases 1\u20133, observations made by the NGEE Arctic team across a gradient of permafrost landscapes in Arctic Alaska improved the representation of tundra processes in the land surface component of E3SM (the E3SM Land Model, ELM). Model improvements emphasized unique aspects of permafrost environments and explored reductions in model complexity while retaining predictive power. The Arctic-informed ELM developed by NGEE Arctic has been used to make novel predictions on processes ranging from permafrost thaw to soil biogeochemical cycling to Earth system feedbacks associated with the unique characteristics of tundra plants. In Phase 4, the NGEE Arctic team is evaluating our new predictive understanding under novel conditions across the Arctic domain. In collaboration with partners at long-term pan-Arctic research sites we are examining whether an Arctic-informed ELM can faithfully simulate interactions among surface and subsurface processes at site, regional, and pan-Arctic scales. In turn, we are using variety of tools to dynamically extend and evaluate ELM inference, with an emphasis on data synthesis and pan-Arctic model evaluation, reintegration of code with an evolving E3SM, scaling across heterogeneous Arctic landscapes, and the appropriate representation of the impacts of increasingly frequent Arctic disturbances.",

        "description": "From August 8 through August 16 of 2021, airborne remote sensing data was collected by the National Center for Airborne Laser Mapping (NCALM) in collaboration with NGEE Arctic scientists. A Robinson R44 II helicopter with a RIEGL VQ-580 II airborne laser scanner was used to collect the LiDAR point cloud data for each study site. A Phase One iXM-RS100F camera was integrated with the Riegl sensor to collect RGB imagery. This data package contains LiDAR point clouds (.las), RGB imagery (tif), 1 m or 50 cm Digital Elevation Models (.tif) generated from the LiDAR data, and shapefiles of the .las tiling system for each site (.shp). Two supplemental documents are also included in the package: 1) a report describing data collection details, GNSS corrections, and processing steps and 2) a document describing the LiDAR Classification used (.pdf). This survey was conducted towards the end of the summer on the Seward Peninsula, and can be paired with data collected in April of 2022 during the snow-on campaign \"National Center for Airborne Laser Mapping (NCALM) LiDAR and DEM data from two NGEE Arctic Sites, Seward Peninsula, Alaska, Winter 2022\" (Singhania et.al, 2023) (NGA314).  The Next-Generation Ecosystem Experiments: Arctic (NGEE Arctic), was a research effort to reduce uncertainty in Earth System Models by developing a predictive understanding of carbon-rich Arctic ecosystems and feedbacks to climate. The NGEE Arctic project had two field research sites: 1) located within the Arctic polygonal tundra coastal region on the Barrow Environmental Observatory (BEO) and the North Slope near Utqiagvik (Barrow), Alaska and 2) multiple areas on the discontinuous permafrost region of the Seward Peninsula north of Nome, Alaska. doe-mcp demo global-climate-archive --output ./demo-output

Add --live to query publishers. No model is called. Live results and availability can differ.

      "A catalog of metadata, not the model output. The files live on federated data nodes and are reached by the access methods each record names; several nodes require a federation account.",
      "Retracted and superseded datasets are in the index and sort first without the publisher's `latest` flag. A retraction is a modelling centre withdrawing output, often for a science error, so the flag is on by default here and both flags ride on every row.",
      "Paging stops at offset 9,999 against 14.7 million records. This archive is searched by narrowing facets, not by walking pages.",
      "Vintage identity is the whole game: CMIP5, CMIP6 and CMIP7 are different archives, and a comparison across them without saying so is the mixed-vintage error the envelope exists to catch.",
      "The index names one fact two ways. A dataset's last covered timestamp is datetime_stop on some records and datetime_end on others, in the same index on the same day. Both are read; a client reading one would report the end of the covered period as unknown for a large share of the archive."

ATB assumptions across editions

Skill: atb-assumptions

ATB 2024: 74.1812 $/kW-yr (2022 USD); ATB 2025: 77.23474920912257 $/kW-yr (2023 USD). These published assumptions retain separate currency bases; no conversion or comparable-dollar difference is calculated.

Read 1 of 1 qualifying rows from ATB 2024; 1 of 1 qualifying rows from ATB 2025. A recorded replay at registry revision 2026-11-21, not current data.

Limits of this example
  • The selection is Class3 Fixed-Bottom offshore wind, 2035 Moderate, R&D, null tax-credit qualifier and 20-year CRP in each edition.
  • ATB supplies scenario assumptions and projections, not observations, bids or project-specific cost estimates.
  • Currency bases differ across editions. A comparable-dollar change requires a documented conversion method and source.
  • PVWatts remains proposed and source-gated. No production model was called.

Download JSON evidenceDownload CSV evidence index

Run this example locally

After installing DOE-MCP, replay without a key, model or network request:

doe-mcp demo atb-assumptions --output ./demo-output

Add --live to query publishers. No model is called. Live results and availability can differ.
